item.title: Breaking: Omotosho, Nwite, 10 others sworn in as Appeal Court Justices
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, on Tuesday swore in 12 new Justices of the Court of Appeal. Among the new appellate court justices whose elevation the National Judicial Council (NJC) recommended at its meeting on May 13 are two Federal High Court judges, Justices James Omotosho and Emeka Nwite, who hitherto handled high-profile cases. Justice Omotosho had on November 20, 2025, convicted and sentenced the detained leader of the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), Nnamdi Kanu, to life imprisonment after finding him guilty on a seven-count terrorism-related charge that the federal government filed against him. Likewise, Justice Nwite, who is handling the N80.2 billion fraud case against the immediate past Governor of Kogi State, Alhaji Yahaya Bello, had on June 3 convicted and sentenced four members of the Al-Shabaab terrorist group to death by hanging for their roles in the June 5, 2022 attack on St. Francis Catholic Church in Owo, Ondo States. Meanwhile, the other justices also sworn in to the appellate court bench by the CJN on Tuesday are Justices Yakubu Abdulhammeed Mohammed, Abodunde Monisola Oluwatoyin, Ajuwa Raphael, Abua Elias Ojie, Ijohor Mbalamen Jennifer, Shuaibu Sabiu Bala, Buba Dauda Njane, Kado Sanusi, Ademola Enikuomehin and Dadom Julcit Veronica. All criminal cases previously before the judges, including the trial of former Governor Bello, will be reassigned to another judge of the court and heard de-novo (afresh). In her address at the occasion, the CJN said the appointments of the new justices brought together “judicial experience from different parts of the country and from courts with distinct jurisdictions and responsibilities.” She disclosed that some of the justices were selected from Gombe, Bayelsa, Cross River, Benue, Kebbi, Taraba and Ondo, following their service at the High Court, the National Industrial Court and the Customary Courts of Appeal in Ekiti and Plateau states. She urged the justices to be mindful that, unlike before when they presided over cases alone, their new assignment would require them to sit with other justices in panels, deliberate collectively and arrive at decisions through a process of judicial engagement. “Your responsibility, therefore, extends beyond determining whether a decision should be affirmed or set aside. You are called upon to promote consistency in the application of the law, clarify legal principles, correct errors where necessary and contribute to the coherent development of our jurisprudence. “This requires a disciplined and principled approach to appellate adjudication. “An appeal is not an invitation to rehear a case simply because another judicial officer might have reached a different conclusion. item.title: Abia records 60% drop in maternal deaths — Govt
item.description: …Renovates 190 PHCs, functionalises 123 …Nursing college gets increased admission quota By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Abia State Government has announced a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, saying the state now has the second-lowest maternal mortality rate in the country. The government attributed the reported improvement to ongoing reforms in the health sector, including the rehabilitation of primary healthcare centres and increased investment in healthcare delivery. Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this during a briefing on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia. He was represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Ferdinand Ekeoma. Kanu said the administration had made progress in its efforts to revitalise primary healthcare, disclosing that 190 of the 200 primary healthcare centres earmarked for renovation under Project Ekwueme had been completed. He said 123 of the renovated facilities had been made functional to provide essential medical services, while 27 had been equipped with solar power, with work ongoing at nine additional centres. The Commissioner also announced the completion of all 77 World Bank-supported health projects in the state. In another development, Kanu disclosed that the Aba Campus of the College of Nursing Sciences had secured an increase in its admission quota from 75 to 120 students following an accreditation exercise by the National Nursing and Midwifery Council. According to him, the revised admission quota was communicated in an accreditation report released on November 13, reflecting the outcome of the institution’s accreditation exercise. Meanwhile, the Rector of Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, Dr Christopher Okoro, has emerged Administrator of the Year in a nationwide poll organised by Leadership Excellence Award. Kanu said Okoro secured 148,267 votes in the exercise, which recognised his contributions to institutional development, human capital development and technical and professional education. He attributed the recognition to developments recorded at the institution under the Rector, including an increase in student enrolment by more than 6,000, improved infrastructure and better staff welfare. The Commissioner also said the state government remained committed to education development, noting that the sector continued to receive 20 per cent of the state’s annual budget. On public health surveillance, the government reported that Abia recorded no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera, mpox or yellow fever during the period under review. The Commissioner for Health, Prof. Enoch Ogbonnaya Uche, who also addressed the briefing, provided an update on the Ebola situation in the country. item.title: Pope calls for ‘less division’ after US midterm elections
item.description: Pope Leo XIV on Tuesday voiced hope for “less war” and “less division” following the midterm elections in his native United States, as he returned from a tour of South America. The first American pope has clashed repeatedly with US President Donald Trump over the war with Iran and made history this month by announcing that he had cast a ballot in the midterms — the first time a pope has been known to have voted. “I would like to see a greater capacity for dialogue, for building bridges, for reconciliation. Less polemics, less war, less division,” the US-born pontiff told reporters including AFP on the papal plane. “I know this is also a dream, but I know it is possible so we shall see,” he said. Trump’s Republican party was handed a resounding defeat in the midterms in large part due to anger over soaring energy prices and the president’s costly war with Iran. – ‘Seeds of hope’ – Leo’s comments echoed his repeated calls for an end to polarisation during his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. The visit, which came less than a month after the 71-year-old underwent lung cancer surgery, also highlighted the social justice priorities shaping his papacy. From the high Andes to the sweltering Amazon, Leo crisscrossed a continent where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary, picking up Peruvian citizenship along the way. Visiting care homes and prisons, the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics reminded political leaders like Argentina’s Javier Milei that economic growth must benefit all, speaking in defence of the poor, the elderly and disabled people. In a lighter moment, the pope joked with reporters about being hit in the face with a rosary bracelet thrown from the crowd as he arrived for a mass in Lima. “The affection of Peruvians — including that person who, with great faith, simply wanted to offer me a rosary — these are things one carries in one’s heart, perhaps in one’s eye,” he said. Asked about his apparent criticism of Milei, he said his comments about Argentina’s austerity policies were “not political” but he encouraged the Argentine leader “to take greater account above all of those most in need”. “I hope that once again we’ve sown seeds of hope, a message of the possibility of unity despite difficulties and differences,” he said. Leo also applied his message of unity to the Catholic Church, which saw periods of factionalism under his predecessor Pope Francis. “What I believe is important in my ministry to the Church is to bring healing, to bring people together. “First let us come together, let us consider what we think the priorities must be, and then we will see how we move forward from there,” he said. – No resignation letter – The visit went ahead exactly as planned despite doubts among many observers after the pope’s surgery on October 13 in which part of his right lung was removed. item.title: Drones Behind Nearly 75% Of Civilian Deaths This Year In Sudan War — UN
item.description: Drones caused nearly three quarters of all the verified civilian fatalities this year in the war in Sudan, the UN said Tuesday. The war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) erupted in April 2023 and is estimated to have killed more than 200,000 people in total. The conflict has forced more than 13 million to flee their homes, creating the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis, according to aid groups. A young displaced Sudanese girl reacts after spending a night with others in Gedaref city, eastern Sudan, on December 26, 2025, after the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) took control of the Heglig area in western Sudan. (Photo by AFP) Out of 2,230 civilian deaths confirmed by the UN human rights office OHCHR to have occurred this year between January and the end of October, more than 1,630 were a result of drone attacks, it said on Tuesday. Drone attacks have “eclipsed the use of other tactics and weaponry”, it said, adding that the full civilian casualty figures are likely to be higher. A Sudanese woman who fled El-Fasher sits next to aid she received at the Al-Afad camp for displaced people in the town of Al-Dabba, northern Sudan, on November 25, 2025. (Photo by Ebrahim HAMID / AFP) Both warring parties have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away. In a report on the human rights situation in Sudan, OHCHR said the first six months of the year were marked by an “unmistakable increase in drone strikes against civilians and civilian objects”. The use of drones has now become “one of the defining features of the conflict”, it said. With the war well into its fourth year, “a robust war economy and steady supply of weapons and other external support enabled the parties to sustain fighting as the conflict continued to spread and evolve,” the report said. The conflict is exacting an “unbearable toll” on civilians, while the prospects for a ceasefire and a peaceful resolution to the conflict remain elusive, it said. Ali Muhammad Ali Abd al-Rahman, a Sudanese national, waits to hear the verdict of the International Criminal Court (ICC), in The Hague, on December 9, 2025. The International Criminal Court on December 9, 2025, handed down a sentence of 20 years to a Sudanese militia leader for war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the country’s civil war two decades ago. item.title: Deputy Senate President mourns late Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau I. Jibrin, has mourned the passing of Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, the Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers. Mr Ajasa passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness at the age of 44, according to the management of Vanguard Media Limited, publishers of the Vanguard Newspapers. In a condolence message issued by his spokesperson, Ismail Mudashir, Senator Barau described the late Ajasa as a thoroughbred professional and one of the finest minds in Nigeria’s digital journalism space. “Femi Ajasa’s dedication and commitment to truth and accuracy set him apart and distinguished him among others. His death is a painful loss, not only to his immediate family, the Vanguard family, but to the entire Nigerian media industry,” he said. The Deputy President of the Senate noted that Mr Ajasa’s journalism journey, which began as a photojournalist with the National Mirror in 2012, through TheNewsGuru and Pulse, to his return to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, was marked by excellence, integrity and selfless service to the country through his noble profession, journalism. Senator Barau extended his heartfelt condolences to the Ajasa family of Ajido, Badagry, Lagos State, Management and Staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) and all his friends and professional associates. “We pray that God will grant his family, colleagues and loved ones the strength and fortitude to bear this irreparable loss, and grant his gentle soul eternal rest,” he said. item.title: Bangladesh Garment Workers, Police Clash In Fresh Wage Protest
item.description: Bangladeshi police fired tear gas and stun grenades on Tuesday in clashes with thousands of garment workers who were protesting after a key wage board meeting was postponed. Protesters hurled bricks, torched vehicles, and blocked the main highway between the capital, Dhaka, and the key financial district of Mymensingh as demonstrations over wage conditions turned violent. The South Asian nation of 170 million people is the world’s second-biggest garment exporter behind China, producing clothes for major international brands including Fruit of the Loom and Levi Strauss. A garment worker throws back a tear gas cannister during a protest demanding increase in minimum wages, in Gazipur city on the outskirts of Dhaka on November 17, 2026. Photo by MD ABU SUFIAN JEWEL / AFP But growing worker unrest over wages that began in October has threatened to disrupt the industry that generates $38 billion in revenues annually and employs more than four million people. Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($240) — a 140-percent increase on the current 12,500 taka, as they struggle to cope with rising food, housing, transport and healthcare costs. Garment workers shout slogans and block roads during a protest demanding increase in minimum wages, in Gazipur city on the outskirts of Dhaka on November 17, 2026. Photo by MD ABU SUFIAN JEWEL / AFP Some 500 factories out of 4,500 are currently shut, sources told AFP, something that is further stoking unrest among workers. “The owners seem unwilling to meet our salary demands. They are already dragging their feet,” said Khanom, 24, who gave only one name. Garment workers look on from a bridge during a protest demanding increase in minimum wages, in Gazipur city on the outskirts of Dhaka on November 17, 2026. Photo by MD ABU SUFIAN JEWEL / AFP In a joint statement, the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) called for a resumption of wage negotiations as soon as possible. The disruption comes during the run-up to Christmas, the busiest export period for Bangladesh’s garment industry. item.title: Why Nigeria’s Credit Market Must Finance Both the Buyer and the Seller
item.description: Credit plays an important role in keeping economic activity moving. For many households, access to credit makes it possible to spread the cost of major purchases over time rather than pay the full amount upfront. This improves purchasing power, supports household consumption and creates demand for businesses across different sectors. When individuals can afford to make purchases, businesses have more opportunities to sell their products and services. However, financing buyers alone is not enough to drive economic growth. The businesses that supply these goods and services also need access to credit to purchase inventory, pay suppliers, manage operating costs and fulfil orders. Supporting both consumers and merchants requires lenders to recognise that the two groups have different financing needs and cannot be assessed in the same way. Lenders must understand these differences when determining how much to lend, the appropriate repayment terms and the risks involved. Chukwuma Nwanze, Managing Director of Credit Direct , highlighted this distinction during a panel discussion at Moonshot. He explained that while lenders assess an individual’s earnings, disposable income, existing financial obligations, and borrowing behaviour, evaluating merchants requires a closer look at their cash flow, turnover, and business growth. A credit market that serves only one side of this relationship risks leaving important parts of the economy underserved. For many businesses, the ability to meet demand depends on having enough working capital. Merchants need funds to purchase inventory, pay suppliers, manage operating expenses and fulfil customer orders. These costs often arise before revenue from sales is received, creating a gap between the money a business needs to operate and the money coming into it. This challenge can become more evident when demand increases. A business may have an opportunity to serve more customers but lack the funds to purchase additional stock or expand its capacity. Delayed access to financing can therefore limit its ability to respond to market opportunities, even when there is a clear demand for its products. Working capital financing can help businesses manage these gaps and maintain the flow of goods and services. It can also give merchants greater flexibility to plan inventory purchases, meet supplier obligations and sustain operations through periods of uneven cash flow. The importance of merchant financing becomes clearer when considered alongside consumer credit. Financing customers’ purchases creates demand for a product, and financing merchants gives businesses the resources to meet that demand. This, therefore, builds a credit market that contributes meaningfully to economic growth. Merchant assessment requires a closer examination of business performance. item.title: 2027: Makinde’s record merits consideration; only Obi can match him — Mark
item.description: …Sees possible alignment between APM candidate, former Anambra governor By Juliet Umeh Former Peoples Democratic Party chieftain, Jacob Mark, has described Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde as a “fresh hand” for Nigeria’s leadership, saying Peter Obi is the only presidential hopeful he believes can compete with him. Mark, who recently joined the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television. He said Makinde’s record in Oyo State deserved consideration ahead of the 2027 general election. Mark said, “His record within eight years, which is seven years now, is something to look at and refer to. The only person that can compete with him is Peter Obi. “I am happy that there is a possible alignment between them before the elections,” he said, adding that “in politics, five days is enough.” Mark, however, said he was not aware of any ongoing discussion for Makinde to step aside for Obi or former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. “I am not sure I have heard that anywhere. I am not sure, because there is no discussion on that that I have heard,” he said. The comments come ahead of a November 23 opposition summit in Abuja. Mark said any alliance should not be made compulsory, arguing that voters should have a choice among candidates. He said, “People have a right to aspire, but Nigerians have the final say. The ballot is in the hands of Nigerians. Nigerians should be allowed to have as many choices as possible.” He said he was backing the APM at the presidential level but would support PDP candidates in Kaduna State’s governorship and other contests. “I participated in the primaries for the nomination of the gubernatorial candidate for the PDP. So I am going to support him,” Mark said. The post 2027: Makinde’s record merits consideration; only Obi can match him — Mark appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Fountain of Life Church removes Jimmy Odukoya as senior pastor
item.description: The Board of Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, has removed Pastor Jimmy Odukoya as its senior pastor, citing a need to enforce the succession arrangements established by the church’s late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya. The board announced the decision in a statement on Tuesday, saying it followed a review of the church’s constitution and the documented instructions left by the founder before his death in 2023. According to the trustees, the review was aimed at ensuring that the church’s leadership succession reflected the founder’s wishes and complied with the provisions of its constitution. The statement said, “Following a careful consideration of the relevant provisions of the Church’s Constitution and a review of the recorded instructions of our beloved Founder, the Board of Trustees has resolved to give effect to the succession arrangements which he made prior to his demise in 2023.” The board consequently declared that Jimmy Odukoya was no longer recognised as the church’s senior pastor, with the decision taking immediate effect. “Consequently, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya is no longer recognised as the Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church effective immediately,” it stated. The trustees described the move as an institutional decision taken in the discharge of their responsibilities and in the best interests of the church. They said the decision was necessary to uphold the church’s constitution, respect the founder’s wishes and protect the integrity of the succession framework he established. “It is an institutional decision taken in the discharge of the Board’s responsibilities and in the best interests of the Church,” the statement added. The board, however, did not disclose the specific succession arrangements left by the founder or announce who would take over the senior pastor position. item.title: Budget 2027: FG moves to slash overhead costs, directs MDAs to share facilities
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief As the Federal Government (FG) prepares its 2027 Budget, it is stepping up efforts to cut overhead expenditure by directing Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to maximise the use of existing government-owned facilities instead of spending public funds on hotels and other privately owned venues for official meetings. The move is part of a broader cost-saving initiative by the Federal Ministry of Finance, through its Efficiency Office (E-Office), to eliminate avoidable expenditure, improve the utilisation of public assets and ensure value for money in government operations. Efe Ovuakporie, Head, Information and Public Relations Unit of the Federal Ministry of Finance, in a statement in Abuja, yesterday, said “the Office is working towards establishing a coordinated system that will enable MDAs to identify and access available meeting and conference facilities across government institutions, thereby reducing the need to hire commercial venues for official engagements.” She stated further: “A major component of the programme is the compilation of a comprehensive directory of meeting facilities owned by MDAs nationwide. The directory, which will be published on the Federal Ministry of Finance’s website upon completion, is expected to provide government institutions with information on available facilities and make it easier to locate suitable venues. “The arrangement will also enable MDAs with under-utilised conference facilities to generate revenue by making them available to other government institutions, while reducing pressure on government overhead budgets.” Ovuakporie said the initiative aligns with the Efficiency Office’s mandate to promote value for money, reduce overhead expenditure, monitor the utilisation of public assets and identify areas of waste across government institutions. The post Budget 2027: FG moves to slash overhead costs, directs MDAs to share facilities appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Customs officers must outsmart smugglers, go intelligence-led — Adeniyi
item.description: Says technology should drive operations By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Mr. Adewale Adeniyi, has challenged officers of the Service to stay ahead of smugglers by adopting intelligence-led operations, deploying technology and strengthening professionalism in the discharge of their duties. Adeniyi, who gave the charge at the inaugural Customs Police Summit in Abuja, yesterday, said criminal networks were becoming increasingly sophisticated, requiring Customs officers to devise smarter strategies to combat smuggling and other transnational crimes. He said the era of relying largely on conventional enforcement methods was giving way to intelligence-driven operations capable of identifying and disrupting criminal networks. His words: “Criminal networks have grown more sophisticated. They use the same routes as legitimate traders to move firearm components, narcotics, fake medicines, protected wildlife and illicit funds, often through digital channels. Our answers must be smarter; they must not be harder.” The Customs boss called for a more professional, accountable and technology-driven Customs Police Unit (CPU) to tackle emerging security threats, combat illicit trade, strengthen institutional integrity and protect the nation’s borders. He charged CPU personnel to demonstrate the highest standards of integrity, stressing that the Service must lead by example before demanding accountability from traders and members of the public. “Before we demand integrity from traders and the public, we must show it ourselves,” he said. Adeniyi also cautioned officers against abusing their enforcement powers, noting that the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023 had conferred extensive police powers on the Service, which must be exercised within the limits of the law. “Authority requires restraint. The NCS Act 2023 gives us sweeping police powers, but every search, arrest and detention must rest on lawful grounds and withstand public and judicial scrutiny,” he said. He explained that enforcement and trade facilitation should complement each other, citing initiatives such as the One-Stop Shop and World Customs Organisation (WCO) instruments, including the Safe Framework of Standards, Authorised Economic Operator programmes, Advance Rulings, Time Release Studies and the Revised Kyoto Convention. According to him, these instruments help reduce opportunities for abuse, corruption and arbitrary exercise of discretion. The Customs boss said the Service had undergone meaningful structural renewal and remained committed to building a disciplined, responsive and professional police unit. item.title: UBA intensifies fight against phishing, scam
item.description: …as 2026 fraud awareness week begins The United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc, has stepped up its fight against fraud, urging customers and the public to stay alert to phishing scams where criminals increasingly use fake bank messages, cloned websites and impersonation accounts to steal account details and money. To this end, the Bank is set to hold the 2026 edition of its Fraud Awareness Week, from Monday, November 16 to Friday, November 20, 2026, with the theme “Fraud Dynamics: Staying One Step Ahead.” UBA’s Group Chief Internal Auditor, Eugene Inotu, who spoke ahead of the campaign, said the bank wants every customer to recognise a phishing or fraud attempt before it causes harm. “Fraudsters are counting on panic. They want you to click before you think, so the strongest defence is to pause,” Inotu said. He added, “UBA will never ask for your PIN, password, OTP or BVN through a link, a text message, an email or a phone call. If a message asks for any of these, it is not from us, no matter how genuine it looks.” Offering practical guidance, UBA’s Group Head, Brands, Marketing and Corporate Communications, Alero Ladipo, urged customers to treat every unsolicited link with suspicion and to confirm requests only through the Bank’s official channels. She said, “Avoid clicking links in messages you did not ask for. Type the UBA website address directly into your browser or use the official UBA Mobile App, and download banking apps only from official app stores’’. The post UBA intensifies fight against phishing, scam appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Pique says Owono’s 12-match ban after De Miguel death is unfair
item.description: FC Andorra’s majority shareholder Gerard Pique criticised Jesus Owono’s 12-match ban following a fatal collision with Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, saying it unfairly blamed the goalkeeper for “consequences that were not his fault”. Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in a Spanish second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding heavily with De Miguel while trying to clear. De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and died the next day, plunging football into shock and mourning. In a video posted to TikTok late on Monday, former Spain and Barcelona great Pique said the Spanish football federation’s punishment put Owono “in a situation that isn’t fair”. “What it does is blame Jesus for consequences which were not his fault,” Pique said in his first public comments on the decision. “I think the punishment should be for the action, not for the consequences,” added Pique, who compared the tragedy in Tenerife to a similar incident which led to a shorter ban. Owono, 25, has said he is enduring the “hardest days of my life” after De Miguel’s death, which Pique described as an “accident” that was “totally inexplicable”. FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said the goalkeeper will decide if and when he returns to football after the tragedy “Jesus will need more than 12 games in order to be available and compete,” said Pique. “No suspension will bring Demi back to us,” added Pique, referring to De Miguel by a popular nickname. Spanish police sources have told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision, a standard procedure for unnatural deaths. item.title: Polysmart commissions 60,000mt food-grade rPET plant
item.description: …as FCMB provides N40bn financing Polysmart Packaging Limited has commissioned a plant with an annual production capacity of 60,000 tonnes of food-grade recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) in Ileke town, Ogun State, with N40 billion in machinery and working-capital financing from First City Monument Bank (FCMB). The facility, which Polysmart describes as Africa’s largest plastic recycling plant, will convert recovered post-consumer plastic waste into food-grade recycled PET materials for manufacturers. It is expected to strengthen local packaging production, support plastic-waste recovery and reduce dependence on imported raw materials. At the commissioning ceremony on October 29, Minister of Environment Balarabe Lawal, said the facility would enhance Nigeria’s capacity to recover and recycle plastic waste while supporting the country’s environmental sustainability objectives. Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun described the investment as a demonstration of Nigerian enterprise, innovation and the opportunities created by a supportive investment environment. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of FCMB, Yemisi Edun, said the Bank’s support reflects its commitment to financing businesses that combine industrial development with environmental responsibility and economic opportunity. “At FCMB, we believe that financing sustainable businesses is essential to building a resilient economy and securing long-term shared prosperity. By converting recovered plastic into new products, this plant shows how manufacturing and environmental responsibility can work together,” Edun said. She added, “Polysmart embodies our commitment to sustainable manufacturing practices, environmental sustainability and wealth creation, reflected in our ₦40 billion in funding for machinery and working capital.” Polysmart Group Managing Director, Wasiu Balogun, said the investment demonstrates the capacity of Nigerian businesses to develop recycling infrastructure that serves local industry and creates opportunities across the waste-recovery chain. “This is climate action made in Nigeria. The investment demonstrates the capacity of Nigerian businesses to develop world-class recycling infrastructure,” Balogun said. He added, “At full capacity, the facility will process up to 100,000 tonnes of mixed plastics annually, equivalent to about 6.5 billion bottles.” The post Polysmart commissions 60,000mt food-grade rPET plant appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NGX Group acquires 10% strategic stake in Nairobi Securities Exchange
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) has acquired a 10% equity stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE), a strategic investment that extends the Group’s participation in East Africa and advances its pan-African growth strategy. The NGX, in a statement stressed that the strategic investment aligns with its priority of building regional leadership through partnerships and African market integration, strengthening its investment presence across West and East Africa. “This latest development builds on NGX Group’s strategic investment in the Ethiopian Securities Exchange (ESX), further demonstrating the Group’s long-term commitment to participating in the development and growth of African capital market infrastructure” the statement added. On the strategic rationale, the NGX explained that the acquisition provides it with exposure to one of East Africa’s most established capital markets, broadening its investment portfolio beyond Nigeria and positioning the Group to benefit from the long-term growth of the region’s capital markets and increasing financial integration across the continent. Commenting on the investment, Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga, Group Chairman, NGX Group, said: “African capital markets are at an inflection point, where integration is moving from aspiration to architecture. Exchange groups that commit patient capital to market infrastructure will help shape how capital flows across the continent. Our investment in the Nairobi Securities Exchange is a disciplined, long-term step in that direction, strengthening the financial linkages between West and East Africa while creating opportunities for sustainable shareholder value.” Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, NGX Group, said: “This investment reflects our strategy to build a more diversified and resilient exchange group with a stronger presence across African markets. Kenya is a cornerstone of East Africa’s financial ecosystem, and our investment in NSE provides exposure to its long-term growth potential while broadening our sources of investment returns beyond Nigeria. Both markets have already shown what closer collaboration can achieve for issuers and investors and a shareholding relationship gives that collaboration permanence. We remain focused on disciplined capital allocation and investments that deliver sustainable value to our shareholders over the long term.” The post NGX Group acquires 10% strategic stake in Nairobi Securities Exchange appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NAFDAC destroys 50,000 fake alcohol bottles in Lagos, uncovers raw ethanol
item.description: … Seizes branded bottles of Jack Daniel’s, Hennessy, Johnnie Walker By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed more than 50,000 empty branded alcoholic beverage bottles uncovered at Iyana Oba, Lagos State, in a major crackdown on the circulation of counterfeit alcoholic products. The bottles, which allegedly were stockpiled for supply to counterfeiters, carried the labels of popular alcoholic beverage brands, including Jack Daniel’s, William Lawson’s, Johnnie Walker Red Label and Blue Label, Action Bitters, Lord’s Dry Gin and Hennessy. NAFDAC Investigation and Enforcement officers, who discovered the stockpile, also found raw ethanol stored in a drum at the location, raising concerns about possible illegal production and packaging of alcoholic beverages using the branded containers. The agency said more than 50,000 assorted bottles were destroyed to prevent them from being recycled or reused in the production and distribution of counterfeit alcoholic products. The discovery has renewed concerns over the activities of counterfeiters who exploit the popularity of established alcoholic beverage brands by using their original packaging to deceive unsuspecting consumers. The practice poses serious public health risks, as consumers may unknowingly purchase and consume adulterated products whose contents, ingredients and production conditions cannot be verified. NAFDAC warned against the trade, storage and use of branded packaging materials for counterfeiting, stressing the need for vigilance and cooperation from members of the public. The agency also urged Nigerians to report suspicious activities involving the stockpiling, sale or distribution of branded bottles and other packaging materials to enable it to take appropriate enforcement action. It reiterated its commitment to protecting public health and preventing counterfeit and unwholesome products from entering the Nigerian market. item.title: ‘Teachers, doctors won’t pay tax when I become gov’
item.description: By Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo LAGOS — Lagos State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Mr. Adedeji Doherty, yesterday, promised to exempt teachers and doctors from paying taxes, if elected governor, saying his administration will use increased Federal allocations to improve healthcare, education and welfare of residents. Doherty, who made the promise during an interview on a Channels Television programme, said he would also introduce a tax card that would enable residents unable to afford the existing tax burden to pay N10,000 annually and enjoy subsidies on drugs and transportation. He said: “When I am governor, I will transfer these palliatives, these subsidies to my people. For instance, the doctors will not pay tax. For instance, the teachers will not pay tax. Those two groups will not pay tax. “Out of this N250 billion plus, I will transfer it into cards, whereby for those that cannot pay N50,000 per year in tax, I will create a card that you can pay N10,000 per year in tax, but you will get a subsidy in your drugs and you will get a subsidy in your transportation. “This is giving money back to the people of Lagos State because I have it. Mr President has given it to me and I am giving it to you.” The PDP candidate also promised free education, saying the funds available to the state would enable him to implement the policy. Justifying the proposed tax exemption for doctors, he said: “We need close to about 15,000 doctors in Lagos State as we speak, but right now we have only about 3,000. So, if 3,000 doctors are not paying tax, please give me a break.” He described teachers as critical to the state’s future, arguing that they must receive proper training and support to prepare children for leadership and professional responsibilities. Doherty further condemned attacks on political activities and disclosed that some people he described as area boys had pulled down his campaign posters around Oregun and the Third Mainland Bridge. He said his Director-General had reported the incident to the police, adding that he would visit the Department of State Services, DSS. item.title: Vanguard loses Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: The Management of Vanguard Media Limited announces with profound sorrow, the death of its Online Editor, Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, who passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. He was aged 44. A statement from the Editor, Mr Eze Anaba, said his death is a massive loss to the Vanguard family and the journalism profession. Mr Ajasa was a valued member of the Vanguard family, who made significant contributions to the growth of the company’s digital operations and online journalism. Born into the Ajasa family of Ajido, in Badagry Local Government Area of Lagos State, Olufemi Ajasa obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Mass Communication, specialising in Journalism, from Lagos State University between 2004 and 2009. He further honed his professional skills with a certification in Advanced Writing and Reporting Skills from the School of Media and Communication, Pan-Atlantic University, in 2015. He began his journalism career as a photojournalist with National Mirror Newspaper in February 2012, where he worked until November 2013. He joined Vanguard Media Limited in December 2013 as an online reporter and content developer, serving until September 2016. He subsequently moved to TheNewsGuru.com, where he worked from 2016 to 2021, first as Online Editor and later as Team Lead and Head of Digital Operations. In December 2021, he joined Pulse as Editorial Quality Assurance Manager. Ajasa returned to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, a position he held until his death. His return marked the continuation of a relationship with the organisation that began early in his professional career. The management of Vanguard Media Limited deeply regrets this irreparable loss and extends its heartfelt condolences to his immediate family, friends, professional associates and all members of the Vanguard family. At this difficult time, our thoughts and prayers are with his family. We pray that God grants them the strength and fortitude to bear this painful loss, and that the soul of our departed colleague finds eternal rest. The Service of Songs/Wake-Keep in honour of the deceased will hold at 14 Sylvia Crescent, Anthony Village, Lagos, on Thursday, November 19, at 5 p.m. Other funeral arrangements will be announced by the family May his gentle soul rest in perfect peace. The post Vanguard loses Online Editor, Femi Ajasa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kano govt, Kwankwasiyya Movement clash over attack on Kwankwaso’s convoy
item.description: *Alleged attack fictitiuos – Kano State govt *Kano belongs to all, not those in power, Kwankwasiyya blasts govt By Hadiza Yusuf KANO — Kano State government and the Kwankwasiyyah Movement were, yesterday, locked in a verbal war over alleged attack on the convoy of the vice presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in the state, weekend. NDC governorship candidate in Kano, Aminu Gwarzo, had alleged that during a campaign visit to Bichi on Sunday, the convoy of the vice presidential candidate of the party was attacked by thugs allegedly sent by the state government. The spokesperson for Gwarzo’s campaign, Ibrahim Shu’aibu, said the team had earlier visited Tofa, Rimingado, Kabo, Gwarzo, Shanono and Bagwai local government areas without disruption before proceeding to Bichi where they were attcked. But reacting to the attack, yesterday, the Commissioner for Information in Kano State, Sanusi Tofa, dismissed the fact that there was an attack on the convoy of Kwankwaso in Bichi Local Government Area, describing the incident as fictitious. Tofa, who accused the Kwankwasiyya Movement of fabricating the reported attack in Bichi said: “In an attempt to generate public sympathy, the Kwankwasiyya team has framed itself a fictitious attack in Bichi, no pictures, no videos.’’ Kano belongs to all, not those in power — Kwankwasiyya tells govt Replying the state government, the Kwankwasiyya Movement said Kano State belonged to all residents, regardless of their political affiliations. The movement said the government had a responsibility to protect everyone in the state and should not allow political differences to affect the safety and rights of citizens. In a statement by its spokesperson, Dr Habibu Mohammed, yesterday, the movement also criticised the state government for dismissing the incident as fictitious and accusing the Kwankwasiyya Movement of making up the allegation to gain public sympathy. The statement specifically faulted the Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Tofa, for demanding pictures and videos of the incident, rather than allowing security agencies to investigate the matter. It questioned why victims should be expected to provide evidence before the government could show concern over their safety. “Kano belongs to all its people, not exclusively to those occupying government offices. Its security, peace and democratic freedoms are collective responsibilities that must never be sacrificed on the altar of partisan politics,” the statement said. The movement argued that the responsibility for investigating allegations of criminal activities rested with security agencies, not the victims, accusing the commissioner of making premature conclusions without presenting the findings of any police investigation. The group called on Kano State police command to investigate the incident, establish what happened in Bichi and ensure that anyone found responsible was brought to justice.
